lotl.label: What's Going On With the Leafs
lotl.body: The Maple Leafs are already staring at a familiar October problem - fine stretches undone by a night of self-inflicted damage. Their 3-2 loss to the Senators on Oct. 3 came wrapped in penalty trouble and power-play stumbles, and that leaves Toronto at 1-2-0, fourth in the Atlantic with 2 points and a one-game skid. The top unit still flashed: Kirill Marchenko's first goal in a Leaf sweater came on the power play, but the late chances bled away and the home crowd heard the same old groan. At 65, you know this script - the talent is there, the margin for error isn't, and the details keep biting. Next up is Tuesday against Nashville, and Toronto needs cleaner discipline and a harder net-front game.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Jays
lotl.body: The season died the way too many Blue Jays seasons do - late, uneven, and with too few bats ready when the game tightened. Toronto's 5-1 win over the Reds was little more than a clean closing note on a year that finished 79-83 and fifth in the AL East. Now comes the hard, honest work: deciding whether Ernie Clement's All-Star first half or his .203 second half better tells the truth about second base, and whether the club wants to keep patching or finally upgrade with force. The front office has money coming off the books, and that matters. George Springer's exit would crack open the roster. What matters next is whether the Jays use that opening to add real impact - or spend another winter admiring the margins.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Raptors
lotl.body: The opener showed exactly what happens when Toronto's new centerpiece stays in street clothes - the offense loses its spine and the whole thing looks ordinary. The Raptors fell 129-105 to the Heat in their preseason opener, with Kawhi Leonard held out in reconditioning, and that is the story of the morning, not the scoreline alone. Preseason or not, a team that wants to matter cannot drift through October with its best player parked on the sideline. Toronto now turns to the regular-season dress rehearsal, but the bigger issue is chemistry: who can create when Leonard is shelved, and who can survive the minutes he misses? Immanuel Quickley and the young guards have work to do, fast. Next comes the Oct. 10 matchup with the Clippers in Vancouver - and, more than the venue, Leonard's availability will tell the truth.

lotl.label: What's Going On With the Commanders
lotl.body: The rough edge of this season has shifted to survival mode - and still, Washington found a pulse in time. The 33-31 win over Seattle stopped the skid, gave the Commanders a 1-2 record and a little air in a crowded NFC East, where they sit third and one game back. But this is no clean bill of health. Jayden Daniels is out with the elbow injury that's already forced Marcus Mariota back into the spotlight, Terry McLaurin is trending toward missing today's London game, and the injury sheet keeps nibbling at the roster. Mariota, at least, gave them a spark last week; now the job is to keep it alive overseas. Next comes the Colts in London - and Washington needs another grown-up road performance, not another wobble.

article.title: Commanders Face Colts in London
paragraphs: The Commanders are in London this morning for a 9:30 a.m. ET kick against the Colts on NFL Net, with Marcus Mariota out and Terry McLaurin questionable. Washington brings a 1-2 record into Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where the league's first U.K. game of 2026 kicks off before coffee for most of Toronto.

The Leafs are back in action Tuesday against the Predators after a 3-2 loss to the Senators, with Auston Matthews and Kirill Marchenko scoring and Sergei Bobrovsky stopping 26 shots. The Raptors open preseason Wednesday against the Clippers, while the Blue Jays have moved into offseason planning, with second base among the spots under review for next year.
